claims.text: The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy has high strength but limited ductility and nonuniform deformation under mechanical loading.
Cu is a ductile metallic dopant suitable for addition to the refractory high-entropy alloy.
Adding 2–5 wt% Cu and applying a controlled heat treatment will produce fine, uniformly dispersed nanoscale ductile precipitates at grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary precipitates will facilitate grain-boundary sliding.
The grain-boundary precipitates will act as localized sites for dislocation nucleation.
Facilitated grain-boundary sliding and localized dislocation nucleation will promote distributed plasticity.
The proposed precipitate-mediated plasticity will delay crack initiation and propagation.
The intervention will improve strain-to-failure or uniform-deformation metrics by approximately 20–30% relative to the untreated baseline.
The intervention will not measurably reduce yield strength.
The intervention will not measurably reduce impact-induced energy release.
The beneficial effect should occur under both ambient quasi-static and impact-loading conditions.
The beneficial effect depends on keeping Cu below a threshold for excessive soft-phase formation.
Uniform precipitate distribution produced by optimized heat treatment is required for the beneficial effect.
Excessive dopant content or improper thermal processing may cause deleterious soft-phase formation or embrittlement.
